title: AI stocks fall after Amodei, Altman, and Musk back AI slowdown
excerpt: Nvidia, Intel, ASML, SK Hynix, and SoftBank were among the hardest-hit names as investors weighed the implications of a deliberate cap on AI progress
content_html:
AI-linked stocks fell across Asia, Europe, and U.S. premarket trading on Monday after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a deliberate slowdown in AI capabilities development, drawing support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.

Nvidia stock fell nearly 3% in premarket trading, while Intel stock dropped close to 6% and Micron Technology stock declined around 5%. In Asia, SK Hynix ended the session with losses exceeding 6%, while Samsung Electronics shed more than 4%. SoftBank stock, reflecting that company's position as one of OpenAI's largest investors, fell roughly 10% to 11% in Tokyo. South Korea's Kospi fell 3.3%. In Europe, ASML lost between 5% and 6%, Nokia gave up roughly 8%, and Infineon retreated more than 7%. Hyperscalers including Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet were lower in premarket trading. Data-center infrastructure plays Siemens Energy and Schneider Electric likewise moved lower.

Amodei published an essay on Saturday outlining a three-step plan he called "pacing the frontier," which would embed third-party evaluators inside AI companies, establish shared safety benchmarks and agreed limits on how fast capabilities can advance, and eventually coordinate with governments including China. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.

Altman posted on X on Saturday saying he agrees with Amodei's call to pace the frontier. Musk posted on X that "Dario is right," according to CNBC. In a follow-up post just after midnight on Monday, Altman clarified that pacing does "not mean 'stopping,'" adding that "no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness."

Amodei's essay and the broader debate it reflects emerged from a turbulent stretch for the AI industry. Jacob Coxon, a researcher who had resigned from Anthropic last week, wrote that AI companies are "gambling with our lives," a post that drew more than 150 million views on X and prompted more than 20 lawmakers to call for tougher AI regulation. Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger responded by writing on X that he believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI will "kill all humans" within the next decade. Altman told Fortune in an interview published Saturday that OpenAI would not go public in 2026, citing the safety environment.

President Donald Trump rejected calls for any reduction in pace on Sunday, arguing that slowing down would erode the U.S. competitive edge over China. China's Foreign Ministry described the warnings as "fear mongering," according to CNBC.
